cands.bio: John Garamendi, born in Florida and raised in Mokelumne Hill, California, is a rancher and businessman. He has served in the California Assembly and Senate, as state insurance commissioner, as U.S. Deputy Secretary of the Interior and as lieutenant governor. He has been in the U.S. House since 2009.

controversies.text: Missed 91 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (13.5%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 31, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-16.

As Insurance Commissioner, Garamendi took over failed insurer Executive Life in 1991. It was sold to a French investor group tied to a government-controlled bank, which California law bars. In 1999 he sued the buyers. In 2005 he testified that he was never told and had said the group could not own it. Investors' lawyers said he knew or should have known. The state settled in 2005 for $516.5 million with Credit Lyonnais and related parties.

Says one thing, record shows another. They say: In a January 2018 interview he said he wanted to "make sure every person is identified" and that E-Verify had "not really been enforced." The record: Voted Nay on H.R. 875 (2025), which would make driving while impaired or intoxicated grounds for barring or deporting a person residing in the U.S. without legal permission; it passed the House 246-160.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Teachers Association, Equality California and California Environmental Voters.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from him on data centers, property tax relief for homeowners, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, gun laws, school vouchers or charters, or police pay and pensions. The pages we had do not give the year he came to California, only that he was raised here. They also do not include his response to the criticism over the Executive Life sale.

cands.name: Rudy Recile

money.note: Individuals gave $10,798; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $9,275. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Retired U.S. Army Major (1988–2014) who served as a Pentagon logistics officer. Former U.S. Department of Agriculture employee and owner of a small web design company. Republican candidate for California's 8th District in 2022, 2024 and 2026. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: San Joaquin County Republican Party (2026), among other voter-guide recommendations listed by Ballotpedia.
Yolo County GOP, Solano County GOP and Eastern Contra Costa California Republican Assembly (2024, as listed in his own Ballotpedia survey).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Recile was raised, or the year he first came to California. His campaign materials say he retired in 2014 after a final posting at Fairfield, but a 2024 survey answer says his family had lived in Solano County for 18 years. We found no record of any elected or legislative office. His website mentions working "alongside leaders on Capitol Hill" without naming a role, so we did not count it. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or land protection, restrictions on foreign or investor land buying, homestead property taxes, or abortion. He says he would cut federal taxes, but that is not specific to homestead taxes. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. The 2022 campaign website text on that page was cut off, and the 2024 and 2026 website pages we had showed only the Veterans issue in full.

local.label: Roots 40: Born in Canada, he came to Fairfield, California as an Army officer and stayed after retiring in 2014, about 12 years of documented residence as an adult.

qual.background: Retired U.S. Army Major with 26 years of service, including logistics work at the Pentagon. Former USDA employee, small business owner, and project, product and data manager. No elected or legislative office.
qual.why: He has real military, federal-agency and business management experience, but no governing or legislative office and no verified policy or budget role, which places him at the low end of the range.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said "Money should follow the child not the child following the money" and that parents should have a choice of where their children are taught, with tax credits for school education nationwide (2024 campaign website). He did not state a position on teacher pay.

workers-first.evidence: Listed securing the border and enforcing current immigration laws among the policy areas he is passionate about (2022 Ballotpedia survey).

clean-money.evidence: Said candidates should raise funds only from the citizens they represent and that there should be "No monies from special interest groups" (2022 Ballotpedia survey). He also said individual donation limits should not be capped.

back-police-order.evidence: Listed "Restoring faith and support in our Judicial system and First Responders and Law Enforcement" among his policy priorities (2022 Ballotpedia survey).

second-amendment.evidence: Wrote on his 2024 campaign website that the Left tries to "limit US citizens' ability to purchase firearms," and presented the Bill of Rights as something to defend. Ballotpedia also lists NRA and California Rifle & Pistol Association affiliations.
